book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 51 · Terrorism and CBRNE Events
title: CBRNE Events: Stay Safe, Read the Agent, Treat Within BC Scope

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already size up scenes, wear PPE, triage, give oxygen and use the BVM. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize a CBRNE event and respond without becoming a patient
  2. Spot the nerve agent pattern and the clues for other agents
  3. Know what the PCP adds, and what's outside BC scope

Textbook: Chapter 51, PDF pages 4195–4262
slides.say: Welcome back. Today's topic is one we hope you never meet: terrorism and CBRNE events. CBRNE stands for chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive. As EMRs, you already size up scenes, wear PPE, triage many patients, and support breathing with oxygen and a bag-valve mask. As a PCP, you go further: recognize the kind of agent, explain why the patient looks the way they do, and know exactly what you can add, and what you can't. We'll cover three things: a safe response, the nerve agent pattern and other agent clues, and the PCP's role within BC scope.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天的主题希望你们永远碰不到：恐怖主义与 CBRNE 事件。CBRNE 指化学、生物、放射、核和爆炸。你们作为 EMR，已经会评估现场、穿戴 PPE、给大批伤员分诊，也会用氧气和球囊面罩支持呼吸。作为 PCP，要更进一步：认出是哪类制剂，说清病人为什么是这个表现，并清楚知道自己能多做什么、不能做什么。今天讲三件事：安全的应对；神经毒剂的典型表现和其他制剂的线索；PCP 在 BC 范围内的角色。

slides.title: CBRNE: a crime scene with many patients
slides.body:
Explosives are still the most common terrorist weapon

  • Deliberate, so the scene is a crime scene, maybe still active
  • Many patients, mass decontamination, many agencies
  • Best clue: several patients with the same signs
  • Second clue: what fleeing victims tell you
  • Also weigh threats, the location and the type of call
slides.say: What makes a CBRNE event different from an ordinary hazmat call? It's deliberate. You're working in a crime scene, and the attack may still be going on. There may be many patients needing decontamination, with police, fire and EMS working together. Bombs are still the weapon terrorists use most. To recognize an event, think about recent threats, the location and the type of call. But the strongest clue is several patients with the same signs at once. One person seizing is a medical call. Five people seizing in one room, with no fire or smoke, is something else. The second-best clue is what victims tell you.
slides.sayZh: CBRNE 事件和普通危险品事故有什么不同？它是蓄意的。你在犯罪现场工作，袭击可能还在进行。可能有很多需要洗消的伤员，警察、消防和 EMS 要协同作业。炸弹仍是恐怖分子最常用的武器。识别时要想一想：最近有没有威胁、是什么地点、是什么类型的呼叫。但最强的线索是多名病人同时出现相同症状。一个人抽搐是内科急诊；同一个房间里五个人抽搐、又没有火也没有烟，那就是另一回事了。第二好的线索是伤员告诉你的话。

slides.title: Five first actions, and where to park
slides.body:
Safe scene, safe you→Notify→Request resources→Command→MCI plan
  • Stop at a distance; stage upwind and uphill
  • Don't get blocked in by other vehicles
  • Send units to a staging area, not the front entrance
  • Call hazmat early; expect more than one agent
  • Watch for a secondary device; keep reassessing
slides.say: Once you suspect an event, five actions come first, in order: make sure the scene and you are safe, notify dispatch, request specialized resources, set up or join command, and start your mass-casualty plan. Stop at a distance and look before driving in. Stage upwind and uphill, so gas drifts away from you, and park where you can't be blocked in. Send incoming units to a staging area, not the front door, because attackers may plant a second device where responders gather. Call hazmat early; they may be far away. And keep reassessing: a wind change or more contaminated patients can put you in danger.
slides.sayZh: 一旦怀疑是这类事件，先按顺序做五件事：确保现场和你自己安全，通知调度，请求专业资源，建立或加入指挥，启动大规模伤亡预案。先停在远处，看清楚再开进去。停在上风、高处，让毒气飘离你，并停在不会被堵死的位置。让后续车辆去集结区，不要去正门，因为袭击者可能在救援人员聚集的地方安放第二个装置。尽早呼叫危险品队，他们可能离得很远。还要持续复评：风向一变，或受污染的人越来越多，都可能把你置于危险中。

slides.title: Zones, PPE and contamination
slides.body:
Hot zonewhere the agent istrained, equipped teams only
Warm zonedecontaminationtrained, equipped teams only
Cold zonetriage and treatmentwhere you usually work
  • Anyone from the hot or warm zone is contaminated
  • Cross-contamination: touching a person not yet decontaminated
  • Level A suit + SCBA: hot zone. Level C respirator: cold zone
slides.say: The hazmat team usually sets three zones, which also mark the crime scene. The hot zone holds the agent; the warm zone is for decontamination. Only specially trained and equipped people enter either one. Your place is normally the cold zone, for triage and treatment. Anyone coming out of the hot or warm zone counts as contaminated until decontaminated. Your biggest threats are contamination, meaning direct contact with the agent, and cross-contamination, meaning contact with a patient not yet cleaned. A sealed Level A suit with its own air is hot-zone gear. Level C uses a filter respirator; it's cold-zone gear and useless where oxygen is low.
slides.sayZh: 危险品队通常划出三个区，这些界线同时也是犯罪现场的边界。热区是制剂所在处，温区用于洗消，只有受过专门训练、有装备的人才能进入。你通常在冷区负责分诊和治疗。任何从热区或温区出来的人，在洗消之前都算已污染。你面对的最大威胁是：污染，也就是直接接触制剂；交叉污染，也就是接触还没洗消的病人。全密封、自带气源的 A 级防护服是热区装备；C 级用过滤式呼吸器，是冷区装备，在缺氧环境里毫无用处。

slides.q: You're sent to a subway platform. Callers report several people coughing, vomiting and collapsing. There's no smoke or fire. What should you do first?
options: Run in with oxygen and triage the closest patients
Stop at a distance, stage upwind and uphill, notify dispatch, request hazmat
Park at the main entrance so loading is faster
Start mouth-to-mask ventilation on the first patient who isn't breathing
slides.say: Let's check your thinking. You're sent to a subway platform. Callers report several people coughing, vomiting and collapsing, and there's no smoke or fire. What should you do first? A, run in with oxygen and triage the closest patients. B, stop at a distance, stage upwind and uphill, notify dispatch and request hazmat. C, park at the main entrance so loading is faster. D, start mouth-to-mask ventilation on the first patient who isn't breathing. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检查一下你的思路。你被派往一个地铁站台，报警人说好几个人在咳嗽、呕吐、倒地，现场没有烟也没有火。你首先该做什么？A 带着氧气冲进去，先给最近的病人分诊；B 停在远处，在上风、高处集结，通知调度，请求危险品队；C 停在正门口，方便装车；D 给第一个没有呼吸的病人做口对面罩通气。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Many people with the same signs and no smoke is the classic clue for a chemical release, so safety and notification come first. A turns you into the next patient. C puts your ambulance where a secondary device is most likely, and where you can be blocked in. D is never done in a chemical event: vapour lingers in the patient's airway and can pass to you, so you'd use a bag-valve mask, and only after decontamination.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。多人出现相同症状又没有烟，是化学品释放的典型线索，所以先保安全、先通知。A 会让你变成下一个伤员。C 把救护车停在最可能有二次装置、也容易被堵死的地方。D 在化学事件中绝对不做：毒气会残留在病人气道里传给你，应改用球囊面罩，而且要在洗消之后。

slides.title: Nerve agents: the deadliest chemicals
slides.body:
• Very strong organophosphates, like some farm pesticides
  • Block cholinesterase: nerves keep firing
  • Sarin: evaporates fast; a vapour hazard; off-gasses from clothes
  • VX: oily, lasts weeks; a skin contact hazard
  • Can cause cardiac arrest within seconds to minutes

Farm call, several very wet patients? Think organophosphate pesticide: same signs, same care.
slides.say: Nerve agents are the deadliest chemical weapons. They're very strong organophosphates, the same family as some farm pesticides. They block an enzyme called cholinesterase, which normally switches nerve signals off, so nerves keep firing and organs are overstimulated. Sarin evaporates within seconds to minutes, so it's mainly breathed in, and it off-gasses, meaning vapour keeps coming off the patient's clothes. VX is the opposite: it's oily, it can stay for weeks, and it enters through the skin. A large dose can stop the heart within minutes. On a farm call with several very wet patients, think pesticide: the signs and the care are the same.
slides.sayZh: 神经毒剂是最致命的化学武器。它们是浓度极高的有机磷，和一些农药同属一族。它们抑制一种叫胆碱酯酶的酶，这种酶平时负责把神经信号关掉；没有它，神经就一直放电，器官被过度刺激。沙林几秒到几分钟就挥发成气体，所以主要经呼吸进入，还会持续释放毒气，也就是蒸气不断从病人的衣服上冒出来。VX 正相反：油状，可以停留好几周，经皮肤进入。大剂量几分钟内就能让心脏停跳。在农场出车遇到好几个浑身湿漉漉的病人，要想到农药：症状一样，处理也一样。

slides.title: SLUDGEM and DUMBELS
slides.body:
SLUDGEMDUMBELS
SalivationDefecation
Lacrimation (tears)Urination
UrinationMiosis (pinpoint pupils)
DefecationBradycardia, Bronchorrhea, Bronchoconstriction
GI distressEmesis
EmesisLacrimation
MiosisSalivation

The three B's kill: death comes from respiratory failure.
slides.say: There are two memory aids for the signs. SLUDGEM comes from the military: salivation, lacrimation, which means tearing, urination, defecation, GI distress, emesis, which means vomiting, and miosis, which means pinpoint pupils. DUMBELS has almost the same letters, but it's more useful because of the B: bradycardia, bronchorrhea, meaning the airways fill with fluid, and bronchoconstriction, meaning they squeeze shut. Those three B's are what kill, because nerve agent deaths come from respiratory failure. Miosis is the most common sign and can last days to weeks. But a stroke, a skull fracture or an overdose can also cause pinpoint pupils, so look for the whole pattern.
slides.sayZh: 记症状有两个口诀。SLUDGEM 来自军方：流涎、流泪、排尿、排便、胃肠不适、呕吐、瞳孔缩小（针尖样瞳孔）。DUMBELS 字母几乎一样，但更有用，因为多了 B：心动过缓、支气管分泌物增多（气道里灌满液体）、支气管收缩（气道紧缩关闭）。这三个 B 才是致命的，因为神经毒剂的死因是呼吸衰竭。瞳孔缩小是最常见的表现，可持续几天到几周。但脑卒中、颅骨骨折或药物过量也会出现针尖样瞳孔，所以要看整组表现。

slides.title: Nerve agents: your care in BC
slides.body:
1. Decontamination first, by trained teams
  2. Airway: suction often; secretions flood it
  3. High-flow oxygen; ventilate with a BVM, never mouth-to-mask
  4. Seizures may not stop: protect, keep ventilating
  5. Request specialized help early; transport

The book's antidotes atropine and pralidoxime (2-PAM), and benzodiazepines for seizures, are not in BC EMR or PCP scope.
slides.say: So what can you do? First, decontamination by trained teams, before you touch the patient. Then the airway. These patients can drown in their own secretions, so suction often. Give high-flow oxygen and ventilate with a bag-valve mask, never mouth-to-mask, because vapour lingers in the airway. Nerve agent seizures may continue until death or an antidote, so protect the patient and keep supporting breathing. The book's antidotes are atropine and pralidoxime, also called two-PAM, plus a benzodiazepine for seizures. None of these are in BC EMR or PCP scope. Your strengths are airway, breathing, an early call for specialized help, and fast transport.
slides.sayZh: 那你能做什么？第一，由受过训练的队伍洗消，之后你再接触病人。然后是气道：这些病人可能被自己的分泌物淹死，所以要频繁吸引。给高流量氧，用球囊面罩通气，绝不能口对面罩，因为毒气会残留在气道里。神经毒剂引起的抽搐可能一直持续到死亡或用上解毒剂，所以要保护好病人，持续支持呼吸。书里的解毒剂是阿托品和解磷定（也叫 2-PAM），再加苯二氮卓类止抽搐。这些都不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。你的强项是气道、呼吸、尽早请求专业支援，以及快速转运。

slides.title: Blister, lung and blood agents
slides.body:
AgentClueKey care point
Mustard (blister)garlic smell; blisters 4–6 h laterdecon; airway may swell
Lewisite, phosgene oximeinstant pain; grey skindecon; burn-type care
Chlorine (lung)bleach smell; choking at onceremove; rest; oxygen
Phosgene (lung)fresh-cut grass; edema hours laterstrict rest; watch the lungs
Cyanide (blood)almonds; collapse in minutesstrip clothes; O₂, BVM

Never sniff to identify an agent.
slides.say: Blister agents attack skin, eyes and airways, especially moist areas like the armpits and groin. Mustard is absorbed in seconds, but blisters appear four to six hours later. Lewisite and phosgene oxime hurt right away and can turn the skin grey. Lung agents cause pulmonary edema. Chlorine smells like bleach and causes choking at once. Phosgene smells like fresh-cut grass, irritates little, and the edema comes hours later, so keep these patients at rest; activity makes them worse. Cyanide stops cells from using oxygen and can kill in minutes: remove all clothing to stop off-gassing, then give oxygen and ventilate. Never sniff to identify an agent.
slides.sayZh: 起疱剂伤害皮肤、眼睛和气道，尤其是腋下、腹股沟这些潮湿部位。芥子气几秒内就吸收，但四到六小时后才起疱。路易氏剂和光气肟一接触就剧痛，皮肤可能变灰。肺部制剂引起肺水肿：氯气有漂白水味，马上让人呛咳窒息；光气闻起来像刚割的青草，刺激很轻，肺水肿几小时后才出现，所以要让这些病人安静休息，活动会让病情加重。氰化物让细胞无法利用氧，几分钟内就能致死：脱掉全部衣物防止持续释放毒气，然后给氧、通气。绝不要靠闻气味来判断是什么制剂。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: after decontamination
slides.body:
BC has no terrorism protocol: combine Oxygen, CHF/Pulmonary Edema (its indications include exposure to toxins) and Hypovolemia.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%; high flow if short of breath or in shock
  • Lung agent: at rest, sitting upright, kept warm
  • Assist ventilations if LOC altered or SpO₂ < 94%
  • Blast injury: control bleeding, splint, keep warm

PCP adds

  • Toxic pulmonary edema: consider CPAP on scene if criteria met
  • BVM needed: consider a PEEP valve, start at 5 cmH₂O
  • Shock: IV en route or if delayed
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L; reassess every 500 mL
  • Shock from blood loss: consider TXA
slides.say: BC has no terrorism protocol, so combine the ones you know. On the left is every level, after decontamination: oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, and high flow if short of breath or in shock. For a lung agent, the CHF or Pulmonary Edema protocol fits, because its indications include exposure to toxins: rest, sitting up, warmth, and assisted ventilations if consciousness drops or the saturation falls below ninety-four. For blast injuries, control bleeding and splint. On the right, the PCP adds CPAP on scene if the criteria are met, a PEEP valve starting at five, an IV with fluid boluses for shock, and TXA for bleeding shock.
slides.sayZh: BC 没有专门的恐袭流程，要把熟悉的流程组合起来用。左栏是洗消后各级别都做的：给氧使血氧维持在百分之九十四以上，气促或休克就给高流量。肺部制剂适用 CHF／肺水肿流程，因为它的适应证里就有「接触毒物」：安静休息、坐起、保暖，意识下降或血氧低于九十四时辅助通气。爆炸伤要止血、固定。右栏是 PCP 多做的：符合条件就在现场考虑 CPAP；球囊面罩加 PEEP 阀，从五开始；休克时开静脉补液；失血性休克考虑 TXA。

slides.q: A 40-year-old worker exposed to chlorine has been decontaminated. She is alert and follows commands: RR 30, SpO₂ 89% on a non-rebreather, accessory muscle use, BP 132/84, no vomiting. As the PCP, what do you add?
options: Walk her to the ambulance to save time
Mouth-to-mask ventilation to boost her oxygen
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A forty-year-old worker exposed to chlorine has been decontaminated. She's alert and follows commands. She's breathing thirty times a minute, her saturation is eighty-nine percent on a non-rebreather, she's using accessory muscles, her pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four, and she isn't vomiting. What do you add? A, CPAP at five centimetres of water, then reassess. B, atropine IM for her breathing. C, walk her to the ambulance to save time. D, mouth-to-mask ventilation to boost her oxygen. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名四十岁、接触氯气的工人已经洗消。她清醒、能听从指令，呼吸每分钟三十次，戴非重复呼吸面罩下血氧百分之八十九，在用辅助呼吸肌，血压一百三十二比八十四，没有呕吐。你要加做什么？A 上 CPAP，从五厘米水柱开始，然后复评；B 肌注阿托品改善呼吸；C 让她走到救护车上以节省时间；D 口对面罩通气提高血氧。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A. She meets the BC CPAP criteria: thirteen or older, awake, breathing over twenty-four, a saturation under ninety-four on oxygen, and accessory muscle use, with no vomiting and a systolic above ninety. Start at five and go up by two point five, to a maximum of ten. B is wrong: atropine isn't in BC EMR or PCP scope, and it doesn't treat lung agents. C is wrong because exertion worsens lung-agent injury. D risks cross-contamination; if she needs ventilations, use a bag-valve mask.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A。她符合 BC 的 CPAP 条件：十三岁以上、清醒、呼吸频率超过二十四、吸氧下血氧低于九十四、使用辅助呼吸肌，而且没有呕吐、收缩压高于九十。从五开始，每次加二点五，最高到十。B 错：阿托品不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内，也不治疗肺部制剂。C 错：用力会加重肺部制剂造成的损伤。D 有交叉污染风险；如果需要通气，用球囊面罩。

slides.title: Biological agents: the slow attack
slides.body:
• Hard to detect; early signs look like flu
  • Incubation: patients may spread disease before symptoms
  • Smallpox: all lesions at the same stage; face and limbs first
  • Inhaled anthrax: like a bad cold, then respiratory failure
  • Pneumonic plague spreads person to person; bubonic doesn't
  • Botulinum: paralysis moving down; ricin: no antidote
slides.say: Biological agents are hard to detect, and early signs look like flu, so the first warning may be many calls for unexplained flu in one area. During the incubation period, people may spread disease before they feel sick. Smallpox is highly contagious; its blisters are all at the same stage and start on the face and limbs. Inhaled anthrax starts like a bad cold, then causes respiratory failure; untreated, about ninety percent die. Pneumonic plague spreads from person to person; bubonic plague doesn't. Botulinum toxin causes paralysis that moves down from the face, so be ready to ventilate. Ricin has no antidote and no vaccine.
slides.sayZh: 生物制剂很难检测，早期症状像流感，所以最早的警报可能是某一地区突然多了很多「不明原因流感」的呼叫。在潜伏期，人还没觉得不舒服，可能就已经在传播疾病。天花传染性很强，皮疹全部处在同一阶段，先出现在面部和四肢。吸入性炭疽开始像重感冒，然后导致呼吸衰竭，不治疗约百分之九十会死亡。肺鼠疫能人传人，腺鼠疫不会。肉毒毒素引起从面部往下发展的麻痹，所以要准备好通气。蓖麻毒素没有解药，也没有疫苗。

slides.title: Radiation: time, distance, shielding
slides.body:
Timeless time, less dosethe dose adds up
Distancea few steps help a lotstage far enough away
Shieldingconcrete, buildingsassume the strongest type
  • Penetration: alpha < beta < gamma < neutron
  • Dirty bomb: injures like the bomb alone; its weapon is fear
  • Irradiated ≠ radioactive; contaminated → decontaminate first
slides.say: Radiation can't be seen or smelled, and EMS has no suit that blocks it. Protect yourself with time, distance and shielding. Spend as little time near the source as possible, because the dose adds up. Move away; even a few steps cut exposure a lot. Put concrete or a building between you and the source, and assume the strongest type. Alpha is stopped by paper or skin, beta by clothing, gamma by lead or concrete, and neutrons only by metres of concrete. A dirty bomb hurts mainly through its blast; its real weapon is fear. An irradiated patient isn't radioactive. A patient with radioactive dust on them is contaminated: hazmat cleans them first.
slides.sayZh: 辐射看不见也闻不到，EMS 也没有能挡住它的防护服。用时间、距离、屏蔽来保护自己：尽量缩短在辐射源附近的时间，因为剂量会累积；走远一点，哪怕几步也能大大减少暴露；在你和辐射源之间隔上混凝土或建筑物，并按最强的辐射来防。α 射线一张纸或皮肤就能挡住，β 射线需要一层衣物，γ 射线需要铅或混凝土，中子要好几米混凝土才挡得住。脏弹伤人主要靠爆炸本身，它真正的武器是恐慌。只受过照射的病人没有放射性；身上沾着放射性粉尘的病人才算被污染，要先由危险品人员洗消。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Decontaminate before the IV: a needle through dirty skin is a way in
  • CPAP: not with vomiting, decreased LOC or systolic < 90
  • Nerve agents: vomiting and secretions rule out CPAP; suction + BVM
  • Mustard, phosgene: delayed; looks well ≠ is well
  • Severe phosgene can drop the BP: reassess lungs every 500 mL
  • Strip all clothing: off-gassing can fill your ambulance
slides.say: Now the new watch-outs for you as a PCP. Your IV needle is a new way in for an agent, so decontamination always comes before the needle. CPAP is a new tool, but BC rules it out with vomiting, decreased consciousness or a systolic under ninety. Nerve agent patients vomit and flood their airways, so for them it's suction and a bag-valve mask. Mustard and phosgene are delayed: looking well isn't being well. Severe phosgene can pull so much fluid into the lungs that the pressure falls; if you give a bolus, listen to the lungs every five hundred millilitres. And strip all clothing before loading.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲你作为 PCP 新要注意的事。静脉针是毒剂进入人体的新通道，所以一定先洗消、再扎针。CPAP 是新工具，但 BC 规定呕吐、意识下降或收缩压低于九十时不能用。神经毒剂的病人会呕吐、气道被分泌物淹没，对他们要用吸引加球囊面罩。芥子气和光气起效延迟：看着没事不等于真没事。严重的光气中毒会把大量液体拉进肺里，导致血压下降；如果补液，每五百毫升听一次肺。上车前要脱掉全部衣物。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Not in BC EMR/PCP scope: atropine, pralidoxime, benzodiazepines
  • Not BC exam drugs: hydroxocobalamin, other cyanide kits, BAL
  • Book's early IV: in BC, EMRs have no IV; PCP IV per protocol
  • Book's steroids for lung agents → BC dexamethasone: croup, asthma/COPD
  • CPAP: age 13+, awake, RR > 24, SpO₂ < 94% on O₂, accessory muscles
slides.say: For the BC exam: atropine, pralidoxime, and benzodiazepines for seizures are not in BC EMR or PCP scope. Hydroxocobalamin and the other cyanide kit drugs, and the lewisite antidote BAL, are not among the eighteen BC exam drugs. Where the book says start an IV early, remember that in BC only the PCP has IV access, under a protocol. The book mentions steroids for lung agents, but BC's dexamethasone is only for croup and for bronchospasm from asthma or COPD. And know the CPAP criteria: thirteen or older, awake, breathing over twenty-four, saturation under ninety-four on oxygen, and accessory muscle use.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要点：阿托品、解磷定，以及止抽搐的苯二氮卓类，都不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。羟钴胺和其他氰化物解毒药，还有路易氏剂的解毒剂 BAL，都不在 BC 十八种考试药物里。书上说尽早开静脉，但在 BC 只有 PCP 有静脉通路权限，而且要按流程来。书里提到肺部制剂可用激素，但 BC 的地塞米松只用于哮吼，以及哮喘或 COPD 引起的支气管痉挛。还要记住 CPAP 的条件：十三岁以上、清醒、呼吸频率超过二十四、吸氧下血氧低于九十四、使用辅助呼吸肌。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Many patients, same signs: stop, stage upwind, call for help
  2. DUMBELS: the B's kill. Decontaminate, suction, oxygen, BVM
  3. PCP adds CPAP, PEEP, IV, TXA; the antidotes aren't yours

Next: Chapter 52, Rescue Awareness and Operations
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: when many patients show the same signs, stop. Stage upwind and uphill, notify dispatch and call for specialized help; you can't help anyone if you become a patient. Two: DUMBELS. The three B's, bradycardia, bronchorrhea and bronchoconstriction, are what kill, so after decontamination your care is suction, oxygen and a bag-valve mask. Three: as a PCP you add CPAP, PEEP, IV fluids and TXA where a BC protocol fits, but the book's antidotes are not yours. Next, Chapter 52: rescue awareness and operations. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，多名病人出现相同症状时，停下来：在上风、高处集结，通知调度，请求专业支援；你自己变成伤员就帮不了任何人。二，DUMBELS：三个 B——心动过缓、支气管分泌物增多、支气管收缩——才是致命的，所以洗消之后你的处置是吸引、给氧、球囊面罩。三，作为 PCP，在符合 BC 流程时你可以加上 CPAP、PEEP、静脉补液和 TXA，但书里的解毒剂不归你用。下一章是第 52 章「救援认知与行动」。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
